mer queries. Hence, customers will be provided with a more relevant
search result.

Different Types of AI
Artificial Intelligence is growing rapidly that some technology once
viewed as AI may no longer be considered an AI. To differentiate AI by
their ability, AI is divided into two types: Strong and Weak AI. Accor-
ding to IBM, Weak AI or Narrow AI is specific type of AI that focuses
on performing some specific tasks, such as answering questions based
on user input or playing chess. Autonomous vehicles, Siri and Face ID
are examples of Weak AI. Actually, all AI that exists today are Weak AI
because they are designed to operate within a limited range of functions
and are unable to expand their capabilities on their own.
Strong AI, or Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), is a theoretical
form of AI that mimics human brain capabilities and is able to behave
like a human, such as learning things from experience, planning future
actions, and having a self-aware consciousness. Unlike Weak AI, Strong
AI can perform much more complex and broader tasks rather than one
specific problem. This kind of AI has gained notoriety because it is
often depicted in mainstream media as a super intelligent robot whose
mission is to take over the world.
As striking as it sounds, conscious AI has yet to be realized. Ex-
pert opinions vary; according to a survey by Emerj, 45% of respondents
think that AGI will happen before 2060, while 34% predicted a date af-
ter 2060. However, many experts also argue that computers will never
become truly conscious.

There are growing concerns about whether AI can think and become
conscious. The Sophia robot is one example of how AI is becoming
more sophisticated and human-like, raising questions about the nature
of AI and its potential impact on humanity.

after an AI-powered educational robot, designed to teach children to
play chess, grabbed his hand and wouldn’t let go.
This incident highlights the risk of physical harm posed by AI-
powered devices, especially when they are not designed or programmed
properly. But the question of whether AI can think or become conscious
is a complex one. While current AI technology is not truly “thinking”
or “conscious” in the same way that humans are, some experts believe
that there is a possibility that AI could eventually reach a point where
it is self-aware and able to make decisions based on its own desires and
goals, rather than simply following pre-programmed rules.
If AI can achieve consciousness, this could be the time when it takes
over 100% of humans. This raises serious ethical concerns about the po-
tential for AI to become uncontrollable and even hostile toward humans.
